Shenzhen (Yantian).event: JMA TC2621 (unnamed South China Sea depression)
Shenzhen (Yantian).note: Operations normal. JMA has the depression slow-moving off western Guangdong at 21.0N 110.4E and forecast to strengthen to tropical-storm strength and track east across the northern South China Sea, passing about 275 km south of Yantian in roughly 45 hours. No terminal has announced a suspension and no typhoon signal is in force as of the 30 Aug 22:05 UTC advisory.
Shenzhen (Yantian).source: JMA specifications for TC2621, issued 31 Aug 2026 07:05 JST

Xiamen.event: JMA TC2621 (unnamed South China Sea depression)
Xiamen.note: Operations normal. The same depression is forecast to reach the approaches to the Taiwan Strait in about 69 hours, closest approach roughly 221 km from Xiamen, by which point JMA has it weakening back to depression strength. Nothing announced by the port.
Xiamen.source: JMA specifications for TC2621, issued 31 Aug 2026 07:05 JST

remarks: Three systems are active but only one is anywhere near a tracked port: an unnamed depression sitting off western Guangdong, forecast to cross the northern South China Sea eastward past Yantian and then Xiamen over the next three days. Bang-lang and Etau are both far out in the open Pacific east of Japan and threaten nothing.
Haiphong is inside the 600 km ring at 382 km but the system is drifting away from it, so no port entry has been opened there.
Shanghai and Ningbo are still working through the Saudel and Dolphin backlog, but the weather side finished on 30 Aug and this entry expires from the page after 1 Sep.
Linerlytica has published no congestion snapshot since 23 Aug, so the queue figures behind the threat ranking are a week old.
